# Bitcraze Crazyflie 2 Nano-Quadcopter

<p class="sr-chips"><span class="sr-chip sr-chip-family" data-family="aerial">Aerial</span><span class="sr-chip">1 joints</span><span class="sr-chip sr-chip-sim">sim</span><span class="sr-chip sr-chip-real">real</span><span class="sr-chip sr-chip-driver">driver: strands</span></p>

You have `crazyflie` in a MuJoCo world after one line, and the same object on the hardware with `mode="real"`.

<robot-viewer name="crazyflie"></robot-viewer>

```python
from strands_robots import Robot

robot = Robot("crazyflie")
```

Real hardware, one line per driver that builds it (needs the robot on the wire):

```python title="sketch"
robot = Robot("crazyflie", mode="real", port="radio://0/80/2M/E7E7E7E7E7")  # CrazyflieDriver
```

Aliases `Robot()` accepts: `cf2`, `bitcraze_crazyflie`.

## Hardware

**`CrazyflieDriver`** (the default for this robot) speaks CRTP over a Crazyradio through `cflib`. Source: `strands_robots/drivers/crazyflie.py`.

| | |
|---|---|
| `port=` | `"radio://<dongle>/<channel>/<rate>/<address>"` or `"usb://0"` |
| SDK | `pip install 'strands-robots[crazyflie]'` |
| Other kwargs | `setpoint_hz=20` |
| Action keys | twists in SI (`wz` in rad/s, converted to the wire's degrees per second in one place) |

What the driver checks before it writes:

- a setpoint is a subscription: the driver re-sends the last accepted setpoint at `setpoint_hz` because the firmware cuts thrust when the stream goes quiet
- `send_action` returns once the setpoint is latched, not when motion ends
- stopping and landing are different verbs
